children: fell in early trading on Thursday after reporting fiscal first-quarter revenue of $3.2B, which was up 6.7% from last year's tally but missed the consensus expectation by $10M.

Blended same-restaurant sales for the quarter increased 3.1% on a fiscal calendar basis and increased 3.2% on a comparable calendar basis. On a comparable calendar basis, the Olive Garden chain saw same-restaurant sales of +1.1%, the LongHorn Steakhouse recorded same-restaurant sales of +6.2%, and the fine dining segment had same-restaurant sales of +1.6%.
improved profit in every segment. However, net earnings were down from a year ago as other expenses were factored in.

"The performance across our portfolio reinforces the importance of having distinctive brands, each with a clear strategy, supported by Darden's scale and other competitive advantages," updated CEO Rick Cardenas. "Looking ahead, our focus remains the same: operate our restaurants at a high level, strengthen guest loyalty, invest in our people and brands, and deploy capital in ways that support long-term shareholder value," he added.

During the quarter, the company repurchased approximately 1.1M shares of its stock for a total of $222.3M. As of the end of FQ1, the company had $1.3B remaining under the current $1.5B repurchase authorization.
Looking ahead, the restaurant company reaffirmed prior guidance for FY27 for EPS of $11.10 to $11.35. The midpoint of the range of $11.225 is below the consensus estimate of $1.29.

title: Darden Restaurants slips after FQ1 revenue falls short of expectations
